bull_bear.body:
- Debt-free; disciplined capital allocation the recurring theme — added ~90k-1L sqft over the original IPO target on the same funds.
- Rationalizing chronically weak KLM Fashion Mall stores (inventory transferred to other KLM stores; manpower redeployed to new stores) rather than persisting.
- IPO proceeds to be fully deployed by Sep-2026 (incl. warehouse).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **SSSG trajectory:** -7% in Q1; the 12-15% revenue guide leans on new-store area, so full-year SSSG may only be ~0 to slightly positive (an analyst pressed this; management concedes it's aiming ~2-3% positive SSSG and calls the guide conservative).
- **Weather/agri income:** ~75% of revenue from monsoon-sensitive AP/TG/Karnataka; poor/erratic rainfall or flooding dents wedding/festive spend (impact usually shows in Q2/Q3, hard to quantify).
- **Geopolitics/war → input costs:** higher fuel and dyeing costs pressuring the supply chain; risk to the ~42% GM defense.
- **KLM Fashion Mall drag:** Telangana-heavy value format still degrowing; a 2nd store closure possible.
- **Discretionary demand softness:** industry-wide cautious consumer; recovery hinges on H2 festive/wedding pickup (Sravana Masam onward).
- **Seasonality optics:** quarterly numbers structurally lumpy (Dasara moved Q2→Q3); reported Q1 looks worse in isolation.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - CEO Bharadwaj Rachamadugu candid and consistent — repeatedly steers investors to a full-year lens, owns the -7.5% SSSG, distinguishes calendar shift from underlying health, and gives a conservative (not sandbagged) full-year frame. Willingly engaged a pointed analyst challenge that the revenue guide implies ~flat SSSG. CFO Sarma precise on cost/seasonality (employee-cost bridge, store-maturity accounting, warehouse timing). Tone measured, disciplined on discounting (proud of ~95-96% full-price), disciplined on channel (won't chase marketplaces). Minor governance note: Chairman/MD absent again — flagged by an investor; management committed him for the H1 call.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The flat headline hides a real ~7.5% same-store decline offset by aggressive space addition — so revenue "held" only because 14 net stores were added YoY; the organic consumer signal is genuinely soft this quarter.
- KLM Fashion Mall (value format) is the problem child dragging blended SSSG and forcing the first store closure; the premium/family formats (Kalamandir, Varamahalakshmi, Valli) are healthier — a mix story, not a franchise-wide demand collapse.
- The jewellery-vs-ethnic-wear dichotomy is the most investable read-through: management concedes jewellery grew 35-40% on a high base while ethnic apparel didn't, attributing it to gold's investment/metal-appreciation angle — i.e., wedding wallet-share is leaking to jewellers, and ethnic apparel is a pure-consumption category with a Rs 4-5k ticket that can be postponed.
- Deliberate anti-marketplace stance: with ~95-96% full-price offline sales and no manufacturing markup, a 20-45% marketplace fee + high RTO would be margin-destructive — a structurally different (and arguably higher-quality) model than online-first apparel.
- Valli small-format economics are the quiet watch-item: productivity is good but rent-to-revenue is climbing, so the small-store rollout is being paced — a signal that unit economics, not ambition, gate the format.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Strong portfolio of established ethnic wear brands catering to premium, mid-premium, and value-conscious consumer segments
- Extensive retail network supported by a scalable store-led business model and strong brand recognition across key southern markets
- Deep sourcing ecosystem comprising weavers, artisans, manufacturers, and long-standing supplier relationships
- Strong positioning in sarees and ethnic wear categories, supported by heritage, product depth, and customer trust
- Growing omnichannel capabilities integrating physical stores, e-commerce platforms, digital engagement, and customer outreach initiatives
- Experienced leadership team with a proven track record of execution, growth, and profitability
- Strong brand recall and a loyal customer base
- Cluster-based expansion strategy that concentrates stores in high-potential markets before entering adjacent geographies, improving operational efficiency and inventory movement
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Consumer demand sensitivity — Performance is influenced by discretionary spending patterns, wedding seasons, and festive demand, making revenue seasonal and dependent on consumer sentiment.
- Competitive market dynamics — Intense competition in ethnic/apparel retail necessitates strong inventory planning, product differentiation, and customer engagement to sustain market share.
- Talent availability — Sustaining service excellence depends on the Company's ability to attract, train and retain skilled employees in a specialised, experience-led retail format.
- Supply chain / sourcing dependence — Timely procurement from a network of weavers, artisans, and vendors is critical to maintaining product availability and quality; disruption in this ecosystem could affect the business.
- Cost and margin pressures — Fluctuations in raw material, employee, and occupancy costs may impact profitability, requiring the Company to rely on strategic pricing and operational efficiencies to mitigate.
- Quality assurance / brand reputation — Consistent product quality is essential to preserving customer trust and brand reputation across the sourcing and merchandising value chain.
- Macroeconomic and geopolitical uncertainty — Ongoing geopolitical developments and global trade/economic realignments pose unpredictable, continually shifting risks that could affect discretionary consumption and the operating environment.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body:
- **Kalamandir (family/saree-led):** leading the FY27 expansion, especially Karnataka (brand value "significantly higher" than in Telangana); new Karnataka stores are larger-format (~14-15k sqft) family stores, saree-heavy.
- **Varamahalakshmi:** premium format; second lead in expansion.
- **Valli Silks (small format, 3-4k sqft):** scaled to 11 stores by end-FY26; now performs "in the same range of Kalamandir and a little better" on productivity/inventory efficiency, but **rent-to-revenue is running higher** for the small format — next Valli wave paused, resumes Q4FY27/next year.
- **KLM Fashion Mall (value/GT):** the drag — sustained degrowth, Telangana-concentrated; **consolidating 19 → 18 stores** (closing 1 finalized in Telangana; a 2nd under watch). New categories added: **innerwear** (+20% growth expected) and **fashion jewellery** (phased roll-out, started in 2 new Kalamandir stores + KLM); men's/kids' wear under pressure.
- **Geography:** ~75% of revenue from AP + Telangana + Karnataka (agri-income-sensitive core).

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

business.body:
- Describes itself as "one of the largest apparel retailers, particularly sarees, in South India", spanning premium ethnic apparel through value fashion, with the claim sourced to the Technopak Report.
- Operates five differentiated brand formats - Kalamandir, Kanchipuram Varamahalakshmi Silks, Mandir, KLM Fashion Mall and Valli Silks - deliberately laddered by price point so the group covers ultra-premium down to pocket-friendly ethnic wear.
- Stores are "Located in prime / central areas of the cities to tap the purchasing power of customers, with a cluster-based model"; stated cluster benefits are focused targeting of customer segments and demographics, efficient management of stores, effective stock rotations and higher opportunity to cross sell.
- Sells the "Retail Experience" rather than only product - skilled store associates, elegantly designed stores with vibrant entrances and window displays, themed decor and traffic-flow layouts, aimed at word-of-mouth references and higher average business per customer.
- Industry backdrop cited from the Technopak Report: organised retailing share of apparel rose from 14% in FY 2007 to 32% in FY 2020; females aged over 25 expected to grow from 37.6 Cr in 2021 to 45.5 Cr in 2031; "At least 1 saree purchased in over 90% households in South India".

business.body:

- [Listing] The company was "Successfully listed in BSE and NSE" in 2023 (BSE Scrip Code 543989, NSE Symbol KALAMANDIR); it began as a partnership firm on August 10, 2005 under the name and style of "Sai Silks" and was converted from private to public limited in 2009.
- [Board/management] Board is chaired by an independent director, Mr. Ravindra Vikram Mamidipudi; Mr. Nagakanaka Durga Prasad Chalavadi is Managing Director and Mr. Kalyan Srinivas Annam and Mr. Doodeswara Kanaka Durgarao Chalavadi are Whole Time Directors, alongside independent directors Ms. Sridevi Dasat, Mr. Pramod Kasat and Mr. Kunisetty Venkata Ramakrishna.
- [Third-party data caveat] Market-size and industry claims rest on the Technopak Advisors report "Industry Report on Indian Ethnic Wear Market for Women" dated July 12, 2022 - i.e. roughly four years older than this presentation - and the deck itself carries Technopak's disclaimer.
- [Unbound social-media figures] The e-commerce page carries follower/subscriber counts (1.3 Million followers, 595 followers, 376 subscribers, and loose values 1.26, 815.2k, 415 k) whose platform labels are lost in extraction, so no individual social channel figure can be asserted.

latest_quarter.body:
- Gross margin ~42% defended via pricing discipline + mix, despite (a) dyeing-cost inflation and (b) fuel/supply-chain cost from the war. Only ~10-15 bps GM erosion.
- EBITDA margin down ~1% purely on operating deleverage (fixed costs over lower SSSG); expected to recover through the year as new stores mature (store maturity = establishment year + 1 full year) and SSSG turns positive.
- ~95-96% of sales are full-price (an 18-year brand asset); management deliberately avoids marketplaces (Amazon/Myntra fees 20-45% + high RTO/returns would erase margins on a non-manufacturer's markup).
- Employee cost seasonality: Q3/Q4 elevated (bonuses + peak-season temp/valet staff); Q1 seasonally lightest (Rs 52 cr).
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue Rs 375 cr (-1% YoY, ~flat); SSSG -7.5% to -7.8% (KLM Fashion Mall + high base + Adhik Maas ~1 month in-quarter); GM held ~42% (-10-15 bps); EBITDA margin -~1% on deleverage; debt-free; employee cost Rs 52 cr. Store base 83 / ~8.14 lakh sqft / 4 states; +~30k sqft in Q1 (2 large Kalamandir stores, Karnataka). KLM Fashion Mall 19→18 (1 Telangana closure finalized, 1 more on watch). FY27 guide reaffirmed: 12-15% revenue (aim ~15%), ~1,00,000 sqft net adds, EBITDA margin > FY26, GM ~42%, SSSG ~+2-3%, innerwear +20%. New-state entry Pune + Kerala in Q4FY27/early Q1FY28. IPO funds (incl. warehouse) to be fully utilized by Sep-2026.
- _Next Q (Q2 FY27) → check: (1) does SSSG turn positive as Adhik Maas demand lands + Sravana Masam/Dasara(Q3) season builds? (2) Q2 space add ~26-30k sqft; (3) GM holding ~42% vs dyeing/fuel cost; (4) KLM 2nd-store closure decision; (5) warehouse deal closed by Sep + full IPO utilization; (6) full-year 12-15% revenue trajectory on track; (7) innerwear +20% & fashion-jewellery ramp; (8) weather/agri impact showing in core states._

outlook.body:
- Cluster-based expansion strategy: concentrate new stores in high-potential markets before entering adjacent geographies, to build brand visibility, operational efficiency, and cross-selling across formats
- Strengthen omnichannel capabilities by integrating physical retail with brand websites, live commerce, virtual consultations, and social-media engagement
- Deliver differentiated, experience-led in-store retail (distinctive store facades, thematic interiors, trained sales associates) rather than compete purely on price
- Maintain an integrated, technology-enabled design-to-delivery value chain: demand forecasting, sourcing through a network of 4,000+ weavers/artisans/vendors, barcode-enabled warehousing, ERP-driven supply chain, and AI/ML-based inventory and store analytics
- Operate a diversified multi-brand portfolio (VML, Kalamandir, Mandir, Valli Silks, KLM Fashion Mall) spanning premium to value price points to capture different consumer segments and occasions
- Continue prudent, disciplined capital allocation with cost management, standardised store fit-outs, and economies of scale to fund expansion while remaining largely debt-free
- The Company maintains a voluntary Dividend Distribution Policy (adopted June 4, 2022) that aims to balance regular dividend income for shareholders with retaining profits for growth, acquisitions, expansion, modernisation or diversification, seeking to strike the right balance between the quantum of dividend paid and profits retained in the business. For FY 2025-26 the Board has recommended a final dividend of C1.50 per equity share of C2 face value, to be considered for declaration at the 18th AGM.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company opened 14 new stores across formats (7 Kanchipuram Varamahalakshmi Silks including one existing-store extension at Hosur, 6 Valli Silks, 1 Kalamandir), lifting the total store count to 81 (7.85 lakh sq. ft. of net retail space, up from 7.16 lakh sq. ft. in FY25) across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Subsequent to year-end, two further Kalamandir-format stores opened at Davanagere (Karnataka, May 22, 2026) and R R Nagar, Bengaluru (Karnataka, June 5, 2026), taking the tally to 83 as of the report date. Expansion is funded partly from residual IPO proceeds and follows a cluster-based approach of deepening presence in existing markets before entering adjacent geographies. On the warehousing side, the Company has utilised part of the funds earmarked for two warehouses (construction at Vijayawada, Andhra Pradesh and a satellite warehouse at Salem, Tamil Nadu) and has identified a further strategic location at Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu for a new warehouse, with discussions with property owners underway.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's ethnic wear market is projected to grow from USD 22.8 billion in 2026 to USD 32.7 billion by 2032, with ethnic wear increasingly adopted beyond festive/wedding occasions
- Organised retail is expected to reach USD 230 billion by 2030 as consumers shift towards trusted, branded, quality-assured retail formats
- India's wedding industry (~USD 130 billion, ~10 million weddings annually) supports year-round ethnic apparel demand rather than only seasonal/festive demand
- Women, ~49% of India's population, remain the largest ethnic-wear consumer segment, with rising workforce participation and disposable incomes supporting category growth
- Festive and wedding wear market projected to grow from ₹1,033 billion (FY25) to ₹1,767 billion (FY30), a CAGR of ~11.3%, driven by premiumisation and branded occasion wear
- Rising Tier II/Tier III city incomes, improving retail infrastructure and digital connectivity are expanding apparel consumption beyond metros
- Supportive GST revisions have improved affordability in the value apparel segment
- Recent GST revisions have improved affordability within the value apparel segment
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: as Adhik Maas (17-May to 15-Jun, ~1 month inside the quarter, inauspicious for weddings/griha-praveshams) collided with a high Q1FY26 base and a broadly cautious, Dasara moved from Q2 to Q3 this year), and is pruning one chronically weak KLM Fashion Mall store in Telangana. Debt-free, IPO fund utilization to complete by Sep-2026.

open.item: Full IPO proceeds utilization incl. warehouse
Full IPO proceeds utilization incl. warehouse

The Audit Committee and Board approved the proposed deployment of the unutilised IPO proceeds of C39.38 crore (C18.91 crore towards store expansion and C20.47 crore towards warehousing facilities) by September 30, 2026.
Of the C125.08 crore (revised C122.72 crore) earmarked from IPO proceeds for capex towards 30 new stores, C18.91 crore remained unutilised as on March 31, 2026, pending deployment.
Of the C25.40 crore earmarked from IPO proceeds for setting up two warehouses, C20.47 crore remained unutilised as on March 31, 2026, pending deployment.
The Company expects the Kalamandir format to play an important role in future expansion, particularly across Karnataka and select urban markets.

The Company expects the VML (Kancheepuram Varamahalakshmi) format, contributing approximately 52% of revenue, to continue driving growth by deepening presence in existing markets and selectively expanding into new geographies.

The Company has identified a strategic location at Kanchipuram, Tamil Nadu for establishing a warehouse facility funded from unutilised IPO proceeds; discussions with property owners are underway to finalise the transaction.

Savings of C18.91 crore from disciplined capex execution on the 30-new-store IPO objective are proposed to be redeployed to further augment the Company's retail footprint through expansion of additional square footage and new stores, without deviating from the stated objects of the Issue.

drhp.business: Sai Silks (Kalamandir) Limited is a South India-focused ethnic apparel retailer selling sarees, bridal wear, lehengas, and men's, women's and children's ethnic and value-fashion apparel through five distinct retail formats, each targeting a different price point and customer segment. As of March 31, 2026 the Company operated 81 company-owned, company-operated stores across 24 cities in Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry, supported by a growing omnichannel ecosystem of brand websites, live commerce and social-media engagement.
drhp.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company opened 14 new stores across formats (7 Kanchipuram Varamahalakshmi Silks including one existing-store extension at Hosur, 6 Valli Silks, 1 Kalamandir), lifting the total store count to 81 (7.85 lakh sq. ft. of net retail space, up from 7.16 lakh sq. ft. in FY25) across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry. Subsequent to year-end, two further Kalamandir-format stores opened at Davanagere (Karnataka, May 22, 2026) and R R Nagar, Bengaluru (Karnataka, June 5, 2026), taking the tally to 83 as of the report date. risks.note: Performance is influenced by discretionary spending patterns, wedding seasons, and festive demand, making revenue seasonal and dependent on consumer sentiment.
Intense competition in ethnic/apparel retail necessitates strong inventory planning, product differentiation, and customer engagement to sustain market share.
Sustaining service excellence depends on the Company's ability to attract, train and retain skilled employees in a specialised, experience-led retail format.
Timely procurement from a network of weavers, artisans, and vendors is critical to maintaining product availability and quality; disruption in this ecosystem could affect the business.
Fluctuations in raw material, employee, and occupancy costs may impact profitability, requiring the Company to rely on strategic pricing and operational efficiencies to mitigate.
Consistent product quality is essential to preserving customer trust and brand reputation across the sourcing and merchandising value chain.
Ongoing geopolitical developments and global trade/economic realignments pose unpredictable, continually shifting risks that could affect discretionary consumption and the operating environment.

sk.overview: India's organised retail comprises organised brick-and-mortar and e-commerce, with e-commerce the fastest-growing format. India retail was ~Rs 83 trillion in FY2025 (~21% organised) and is projected to reach Rs 123-135 trillion by FY2030. India e-commerce (including quick commerce) is ~Rs 6 trillion GMV (~US$70 billion) currently, projected to reach Rs 15-18 trillion (12-13% retail penetration) by FY2030.
